leads.title: Gender Recognition Act 2004
leads.documents: Core transgender legal status machinery in UK - allows transgender people to change legal gender, obtain new birth certificate and Gender Recognition Certificate (GRC) via Gender Recognition Panel after 2 years transition; surgery not required; marriage/civil partnership interaction.
leads.detail: Cited as Gender Recognition Act 2004 (Welsh: Deddf Cydnabod Rhywedd 2004; Scottish Gaelic: Achd Aithneachadh Gne 2004), in force since 4 April 2005. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Goodwin v United Kingdom (2002) - European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: Court ruling finding UK in breach of Articles 8 and 12 ECHR for preventing legal gender change / birth certificate change; led directly to passing of Gender Recognition Act 2004.
leads.detail: Cited as 2002 European Court of Human Rights case Goodwin v United Kingdom, breach of Articles 8 and 12. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Corbett v Corbett (1970)
leads.documents: Court ruling that made it legally impossible for transgender people to change sex marker on birth certificate and to marry in acquired gender; used as precedent including in US courts.
leads.detail: Cited as 1970 decision Corbett v Corbett. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: P v S and Cornwall County Council (1996) - European Court of Justice
leads.documents: Ruling that European anti-gender discrimination law applies to trans people.
leads.detail: Cited as P v S and Cornwall County Council decided by European Court of Justice in 1996. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Government Policy Concerning Transsexual People - Lord Chancellor's office, December 2002
leads.documents: UK government policy document categorically stating transsexualism 'is not a mental illness'.
leads.detail: Cited as Lord Chancellor's office document published December 2002. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Equality Act 2010
leads.documents: Extends discrimination protections for LGBT people to all areas; basis for anti-discrimination enforcement machinery.
leads.detail: Cited as Equality Act 2010, protections in place since 1999 then extended. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: ILGA-Europe Annual Review of LGBTI Rights - 2015, 2020, 2025 reports
leads.documents: Human-rights institutional scoring showing backsliding: UK highest score in Europe in 2015 (86%, 92% Scotland), 9th place 66% in 2020 with concern about 'hostile climate on trans rights fuelled by opposition groups', 22nd place 45% in 2025, third steepest drop.
leads.detail: Cited as ILGA-Europe's 2015 review, 2020 rankings, 2025 report. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Dudgeon v. United Kingdom - European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: ECHR determination that led to legalization of same-sex sexual activity in Northern Ireland via Homosexual Offences (Northern Ireland) Order 1982.
leads.detail: Cited as Dudgeon v. United Kingdom leading to Order in Council 8 December 1982. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Sutherland v. United Kingdom - European Commission of Human Rights / European Court of Human Rights
leads.documents: Finding of violation of Articles 8 and 14 ECHR by discriminatory age of consent; government undertaking to legislate equal age of consent.
leads.detail: Cited as decision of 1 July 1997, government submission 13 October 1997 to propose bill reducing age from 18 to 16. No URL visible in text.

leads.title: Civil Partnership Act 2004 / Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013 / Marriage and Civil Partnership (Scotland) Act 2014 / Northern Ireland (Executive Formation etc) Act 2019
leads.documents: Laws creating and extending legal recognition of same-sex relationships: civil partnerships (2005), same-sex marriage in England/Wales (2014), Scotland (2014), Northern Ireland (2020).
leads.detail: Cited with dates: Civil Partnership Act 2004 effective 5 Dec 2005; Marriage (Same Sex Couples) Act 2013 in force 13 March 2014; Scottish Act passed Feb 2014 effective 16 Dec 2014; 2019 Act mandated regulations signed 19 Dec 2019 effective 13 Jan 2020. No URL visible in text.
